extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, and prospective IARPA applicants interested in IARPA's mission and program approaches
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of IARPA's stated principles, evaluation mechanisms, and program-level success goals that govern how it selects, runs, and evaluates funded research programs. Useful for researchers or organizations preparing to engage with or apply to IARPA programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-risk, high-payoff research
rubrics_metrics.description: IARPA characterizes its mission as 'To envision and lead high-risk, high-payoff research that delivers innovative technology for future overwhelming intelligence advantage.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are intended to enable researchers to pursue ideas that are potentially disruptive to the status quo; emphasis on ambitious technical goals modeled after the ARPA paradigm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive multi-year programs scored on shared metrics and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: IARPA invests in multi-year research programs, in which academic and industry teams compete to solve a well-defined set of technical problems, regularly scored on a shared set of metrics and milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are structured as competitions with regular scoring against shared metrics; performance against milestones and metrics is a central evaluation mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and external engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Most IARPA research is unclassified and openly published; IARPA's goals of openness and external engagement serve to draw in expertise from academia and industry or individuals outside government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open publication and external community involvement are explicit program design features to broaden participation and leverage outside innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology transition / handoff expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: IARPA transfers successful research results and technologies to other government agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are expected not only to produce research outputs but to produce results that can be transitioned to and adopted by operational government customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term-limited program managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each program is led by an IARPA Program Manager (PM) who is a term-limited Government employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term-limited PMs are part of the agency model to encourage ambitious targets and program refresh; governance/design criterion for program leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tournaments, prizes, and novel procurement mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: IARPA has pursued objectives not only through traditional funding programs but also through tournaments and prizes (e.g., forecasting tournaments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative incentive mechanisms (crowdsourcing, tournaments, prizes) are explicitly used to solicit novel approaches and aggregate distributed judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on anticipatory intelligence and predictive accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: IARPA funds research into anticipatory intelligence, using data science to make predictions about future events; programs aim to improve accuracy, precision, and timeliness of intelligence forecasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forecasting-oriented metrics (accuracy, precision, timeliness) are central for programs like ACE and HFC; human-plus-machine hybrid approaches are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidisciplinary funding across technical and social sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: IARPA funds academic and industry research across mathematics, computer science, physics, chemistry, biology, neuroscience, linguistics, political science, and cognitive psychology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad disciplinary scope is a design criterion; programs often combine multiple fields to address intelligence-relevant problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on operational realism and real-world data
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs aim to develop systems and datasets that operate under realistic conditions (e.g., CORE3D: operationally realistic 3-D environments; DIVA: automate video monitoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success criteria include applicability in operationally realistic scenarios and using commercial/satellite/airborne imagery or other real-world data streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — Aggregative Contingent Estimation (ACE)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACE aimed 'to dramatically enhance the accuracy, precision, and timeliness of intelligence forecasts for a broad range of event types, through the development of advanced techniques that elicit, weight, and combine the judgments of many intelligence analysts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focused on measurable improvements in forecasting accuracy, precision, and timeliness via aggregation and weighting techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — ATHENA (cybersecurity)
rubrics_metrics.description: ATHENA aimed 'to provide an early warning system for detecting precursors to cyberattacks.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success measured by ability to detect precursors and provide early warning in cybersecurity contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — Babel (speech recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Babel developed 'agile and robust speech recognition technology that can be rapidly applied to any human language' to provide effective search capability for analysts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success criterion: robustness and rapid applicability across many languages to enable search/transcription of real-world recorded speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — Biometrics Exploitation Science & Technology (BEST)
rubrics_metrics.description: BEST focused on trying to 'significantly advance the state-of-the-science for biometrics technologies', discovering techniques to utilize biometrics from subjects in less controlled environments producing results comparable to controlled environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation centers on biometric performance in unconstrained/operational conditions versus controlled lab baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — Synthetic Holographic Observation (SHO)
rubrics_metrics.description: SHO's stated goal was 'to enable full-parallax, full-color, high-resolution display of dynamic 3D data without head-gear, and possessing visually continuous perspectives without artifacts over wide viewing angles.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical success judged by display quality metrics (parallax, color, resolution, artifact absence) in a head-gear-free form factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — CORE3D (3-D environments)
rubrics_metrics.description: CORE3D aims to 'develop rapid automated systems for 3-D models which are designed with complex physical properties and automated methods that will pull commercial, satellite, and airborne imagery.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success measured by speed and fidelity of automated 3-D model creation from heterogeneous imagery sources and modeling of complex physical properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — CREATE (crowdsourcing for analytic reasoning)
rubrics_metrics.description: CREATE is 'to develop, and experimentally test, systems that use crowdsourcing and structured analytic techniques to improve analytic reasoning.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation based on experimentally demonstrated improvements in analytic reasoning when using crowdsourcing plus structured techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — DIVA (video analytics)
rubrics_metrics.description: DIVA aims to 'advance state-of-the-art artificial visual perception, and automate video monitoring.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success measured via automated visual perception performance metrics on monitoring tasks (accuracy, detection rate, false positives) in realistic video settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — FunGCAT (biological sequence screening tools)
rubrics_metrics.description: FunGCAT aims 'to develop next-generation biological data tools to improve DNA sequence screening, augment biodefense capabilities through the characterization of threats, and advance our understanding of the relative risks posed by unknown sequences.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success judged by enhancement in DNA screening capability, threat characterization accuracy, and risk assessment for unknown sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — Hybrid Forecasting Competition (HFC)
rubrics_metrics.description: HFC aims 'to improve accuracy in predicting worldwide geopolitical issues ... by leveraging the relative strengths of humans and machines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation via forecasting accuracy on geopolitical events using human-machine hybrid systems; measurable improvement over baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — MATERIAL (machine translation for retrieval)
rubrics_metrics.description: MATERIAL aims to 'develop and deploy fully automatic systems that will allow English-only speakers to accurately and efficiently identify foreign language documents of interest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success measured by retrieval accuracy and efficiency for English-only users identifying relevant foreign-language documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — MAEGLIN (compact environmental sampling)
rubrics_metrics.description: MAEGLIN aims 'to develop a compact system capable of unattended environmental sampling and chemical identification with minimal (preferably no) consumables.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical metrics include compactness, unattended operation capability, chemical identification accuracy, and low consumables usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — MOSAIC (personnel assessment sensors)
rubrics_metrics.description: MOSAIC aims to develop 'unobtrusive, passive, and persistent measurement to predict an individual’s job performance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation concerns sensor unobtrusiveness, persistency, predictive validity for job performance, and privacy/operational considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — RAVEN (nano-electronics analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: RAVEN aims to 'develop tools to rapidly image current and future integrated circuit chips.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success measured by speed and resolution of imaging/instrumentation applied to integrated circuits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific success criterion — SMART (space-based automated recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: SMART is a Space-based Machine Automated Recognition Technique program (goal description referenced but not detailed on the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied success measures include automated recognition performance for space-based imagery/objects; specifics to be found in program documentation.
